learning_objective: 🎯 Become a data analyst! Learn the mathematical tools to find the center, spread, and relationships within geographical data.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Finding the 'average' or center of the data. Mean is the arithmetic average. Median is the exact middle value when arranged in order. Mode is the most frequently occurring value.
Tells you how spread out the data is. Range is (Highest - Lowest). Standard Deviation is the most accurate measure, showing how much the data deviates from the mean.
Measures the relationship between two variables (e.g., Rainfall and Crop Yield). It ranges from +1 (perfect positive) to -1 (perfect negative). 0 means no correlation.
A method to calculate correlation when data isn't exact numbers but ranks (e.g., ranking states by cleanliness vs. ranking them by literacy).

fun_activity.title: 👟 The Shoe Size Average
fun_activity.instructions: Find out the shoe sizes of 5 family members. Calculate the Mean (add them all and divide by 5), find the Median (middle number), and the Mode (the size that appears most)!

exam_tips: 📌 You MUST know the formulas for Mean, Median, and Mode for both ungrouped and grouped data.
📌 Standard Deviation is crucial—practice the steps to calculate it for grouped data.
📌 Spearman’s Rank Correlation formula (ρ = 1 - (6∑d² / n(n²-1))) is a guaranteed practical exam question.
quick_recap: ⭐ Mean is affected by extreme values, but Median is not.
⭐ A positive correlation means as one variable increases, the other also increases.
⭐ Dispersion tells you if the average is a reliable representation of the data.
